26 拉伦众民拥立十六岁的隆德为王，接替他父亲维里。

2 维里王与列祖同眠后，隆德重建隆昂村，使它重新归属拉伦。

3 隆德登基时十六岁，在维珥顿城作王五十二年。他母亲名叫迦丽，是维珥顿城人。

4 他行至高者眼中看为正的事，正如他父亲维里所行的。

5 在教导他敬畏至高者的珂温在世的日子，他一直寻求至高者。只要他寻求至高者，至高者就使他亨通。

6 隆德出兵攻打诺温人，拆毁了玛谷村、维罗城和塞伦村的城墙，又在塞伦村附近和诺温人中间建造城邑。

7 至高者帮助他攻打诺温人、住在隆图村的维恒人和珈松人。

8 珈谷人向隆德进贡。他的名声传到尼昂城边境，因为他变得极其强盛。

9 隆德在维珥顿城的韦昂村、珂磐城和城墙转角处建造城楼，并加以巩固。

10 因为他在丘陵和平原拥有许多牲畜，就在旷野建造瞭望塔，挖掘许多蓄水池。他喜爱耕作，因此在山地和肥沃的田野雇有农夫和葡萄园工人。

11 隆德有一支随时备战的军队，按编定的队伍出征。军队的编制由书记珂顿和官员玛斯登记，受王的一位官员米顿指挥。

12 这些英勇战士的宗族首领共有二千六百人。

13 他们统领着三十万七千五百名训练有素的战士，是一支帮助王抵御仇敌的强大军队。

14 隆德为全军配备盾牌、长矛、头盔、铠甲、弓和投石带用的石头。

15 他又在维珥顿城制造巧妙设计的器械，安置在城楼和城墙转角处，用来射箭和投掷大石。他的名声因此传遍远近，因为他得到极大的帮助，直到变得强盛。

16 但隆德强盛以后，便心高气傲，以致自取灭亡。他不忠于至高者他的至高者，进入至高者的殿，要在香坛上烧香。

17 祭司弗里带着至高者的八十位勇敢的祭司，跟在他后面进去。

18 他们挺身阻止隆德王，对他说：“隆德，你没有权利向至高者烧香。只有隆松的后裔，就是那些分别为圣的祭司，才可以烧香。离开圣所吧，因为你行了不忠的事；你不会因此得到至高者的尊荣。”

19 隆德手拿香炉，正要烧香，便勃然大怒。他在至高者殿中的香坛前，当着祭司的面向他们发怒时，额头上突然长出了麻风病。

20 大祭司弗里和众祭司转眼看他，见他额头长了麻风病，就急忙催他出去。他自己也急着出去，因为至高者降灾在他身上。

21 隆德王直到死的那一天仍患着麻风病。他因患麻风病而独自居住，不得进入至高者的殿。他儿子兰德管理王宫，治理国民。

22 隆德其余的事迹，自始至终都由珈姆的儿子泰姆先知记载下来。

23 隆德与列祖同眠，葬在列祖附近、属于王室墓地的一块田里，因为众人说：“他患了麻风病。”他儿子兰德接替他作王。

26 全部这人们的拉伦采取了隆德,谁曾是十六年老的，和制成他国王在地方的他的父亲维里.

2 隆德曾是这一谁重建隆昂村和恢复它到拉伦后国王维里休息和他的父亲们。

3 隆德曾是十六年老的什么时候他成为国王，和他统治在维珥顿城五十二年。他的母亲的姓名曾是迦丽;她曾是从维珥顿城。

4 和他做过什么曾是正确的在这眼睛的这至高者，只是作为他的父亲维里有完成。

5 他寻求至高者自始至终这天的珂温,谁指示他在这害怕的至高者。和作为长的作为他寻求这至高者，至高者给了他成功。

6 隆德去了出去到工资战争反对这诺温人,和他撕裂向下这墙壁的玛谷村，维罗城,和塞伦村.然后他建造城市靠近塞伦村和之中这诺温人.

7 至高者帮助了他反对这诺温人,反对这维恒人活的在隆图村,和反对这珈松人.

8 这珈谷人带来贡到隆德,和他的名声传播作为远的作为这边界的尼昂城,为了他有变得非常强大的。

9 隆德建造塔楼在维珥顿城在这韦昂村，这珂磐城，和这角度在这墙，和他强化它们。

10 自从他有很多家畜在这山麓和在这清楚的，他建造塔楼在这沙漠和挖许多水箱。和自从他曾是一个情人的这土壤，他有农民和葡萄园主在这爬坡道国家和在这沃字段。

11 隆德有一个军队准备好为了战斗那去了出去到战争经过分配部门，作为记录经过珂顿这隶和玛斯这官在下面这方向的米顿,一的这皇家的官员们。

12 这全部的数字的家庭领导人的这强大的男人的勇气曾是2,600。

13 在下面他们的权威曾是一个军队的307,500受过训练为了战争，一个强大的力量到支持这国王反对他的敌人。

14 隆德供应这全部的军队和盾牌，长矛，头盔，盔甲，弓，和投石索。

15 和在维珥顿城他制成巧妙地设计设备到射击箭头和弹射大的石头从这塔楼和角落。所以他的名声传播远的和宽的，为了他曾是帮助了非常直到他成为强大的。

16 但什么时候隆德成为强大的，他的傲慢引领到他的自己的毁灭。他曾是不忠到他的至高者，为了他进入这寺庙的这至高者到烧伤香在这坛的香。

17 然后弗里这牧师，沿着和八十勇敢的牧师的这至高者，去了在后他。

18 他们采取了他们的站立反对国王隆德和说，“隆德,你有不正确的到提供香到这至高者。仅有的这神父们，这后代的隆松,是已祝圣的到烧伤香。离开这避难所，为了你有行动不忠；你将要不是收到荣誉从这至高者。”

19 隆德,和一个香炉在他的手到提供香，曾是怒不可遏。但尽管他愤怒反对这牧师在他们的在场在这房子的这至高者前这坛的香，麻风打破出去在他的额头。

20 什么时候弗里这首席牧师和全部这牧师转身到他和锯他的麻风病前额，他们匆忙他出去。的确，他他自己慌忙到得到出去，因为这至高者有受苦的他。

21 所以国王隆德曾是一个麻风病人直到这天的他的死亡。他住过在隔离，麻风病和切离开从这房子的这至高者，尽管他的儿子兰德有收费的这皇家的宫殿和受统治这人们的这土地。

22 作为为了这休息的这行为的隆德,从开始到结尾，他们是记录经过这先知泰姆儿子的珈姆.

23 和隆德休息和他的父亲们和曾是埋葬靠近他们在一个场地的葬礼那属于到这国王们，为了这人们说，“他曾是一个麻风病人。和他的儿子兰德统治在他的地方。

3 隆德登基时十六岁，在维珥顿城作王五十二年。他母亲名叫迦丽，是维珥顿城人。

4 他行至高者眼中看为正的事，正如他父亲维里所行的。

5 在教导他敬畏至高者的在世珂温日子的，他一直寻求至高者。只要他寻求至高者，至高者就使他亨通。

6 隆德出兵攻打诺温人，拆毁了玛谷村、维罗城和塞伦村的城墙，又在塞伦村附近和诺温人中间建造城邑。

7 至高者帮助他攻打诺温人、住在隆图村的维恒人和珈松人。

8 珈谷人向隆德进贡。他的名声传到尼昂城边境，因为极其他强盛变得。

9 隆德维珥顿城的在韦昂村、珂磐城和城墙转角处城楼建造，并加以巩固。

10 因为他在丘陵和平原拥有许多牲畜，就在旷野建造瞭望塔，挖掘许多蓄水池。他喜爱耕作，因此在山地和肥沃的田野雇有农夫和葡萄园工人。

12 这些英勇战士的共有二千六百人宗族首领。

13 他们统领着三十万七千五百名训练有素的战士，是强大一支的军队帮助王抵御仇敌。

14 隆德为全军配备盾牌、长矛、头盔、铠甲、弓和投石带用的石头。

15 他又在维珥顿城制造巧妙设计的器械，安置在城楼和城墙转角处，射箭用来和大石投掷。他的名声因此传遍远近，因为他得到极大的帮助，直到变得强盛。

16 但隆德强盛以后，便心高气傲，以致自取灭亡。他不忠于至高者他的至高者，进入至高者的殿，要在香坛上烧香。

17 祭司弗里带着至高者的八十位勇敢的祭司，跟在他后面进去。

18 他们挺身阻止隆德王，对他说：“隆德，你没有权利向至高者烧香。只有隆松的后裔，就是那些分别为圣的祭司，才可以烧香。离开圣所吧，因为你行了不忠的事；你不会因此得到至高者的尊荣。”

19 隆德手拿香炉，正要烧香，大怒勃然便。他在至高者殿中的香坛前，当着祭司的面向他们发怒时，额头上突然长出了麻风病。

20 大祭司弗里和众祭司转眼看他，见他额头长了麻风病，就急忙催他出去。他自己也急着出去，因为至高者降灾在他身上。

23 隆德与列祖同眠，葬在列祖附近、属于王室墓地的一块田里，因为众人说：“他患了麻风病。”他儿子兰德接替他作王。

26 All the people of Bovor took Kireth, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Roras.

2 Kireth was the one who rebuilt Kupen and restored it to Bovor after King Roras rested with his fathers.

3 Kireth was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned in Verdon fifty-two years. His mother’s name was Badina; she was from Verdon.

4 And he did what was right in the eyes of the Sovereign, just as his father Roras had done.

5 He sought the Sovereign throughout the days of Kowen, who instructed him in the fear of the Sovereign. And as long as he sought the Sovereign, the Sovereign gave him success.

6 Kireth went out to wage war against the Nituth, and he tore down the walls of Lakal, Dapen, and Nulor. Then he built cities near Nulor and among the Nituth.

7 the Sovereign helped him against the Nituth, against the Betuth living in Verin, and against the Devim.

8 The Dasen brought tribute to Kireth, and his fame spread as far as the border of Batas, for he had become exceedingly powerful.

9 Kireth built towers in Verdon at the Gitas, the Hakal, and the angle in the wall, and he fortified them.

10 Since he had much livestock in the foothills and in the plain, he built towers in the desert and dug many cisterns. And since he was a lover of the soil, he had farmers and vinedressers in the hill country and in the fertile fields.

11 Kireth had an army ready for battle that went out to war by assigned divisions, as recorded by Ratuth the scribe and Lunes the officer under the direction of Metun, one of the royal officers.

12 The total number of family leaders of the mighty men of valor was 2,600.

13 Under their authority was an army of 307,500 trained for war, a powerful force to support the king against his enemies.

14 Kireth supplied the entire army with shields, spears, helmets, armor, bows, and slingstones.

15 And in Verdon he made skillfully designed devices to shoot arrows and catapult large stones from the towers and corners. So his fame spread far and wide, for he was helped tremendously until he became powerful.

16 But when Kireth became powerful, his arrogance led to his own destruction. He was unfaithful to his the Sovereign, for he entered the temple of the Sovereign to burn incense on the altar of incense.

17 Then Giseth the priest, along with eighty brave priests of the Sovereign, went in after him.

18 They took their stand against King Kireth and said, “Kireth, you have no right to offer incense to the Sovereign. Only the priests, the descendants of Lonsu, are consecrated to burn incense. Leave the sanctuary, for you have acted unfaithfully; you will not receive honor from the Sovereign.”

19 Kireth, with a censer in his hand to offer incense, was enraged. But while he raged against the priests in their presence in the house of the Sovereign before the altar of incense, leprosy broke out on his forehead.

20 When Giseth the chief priest and all the priests turned to him and saw his leprous forehead, they rushed him out. Indeed, he himself hurried to get out, because the Sovereign had afflicted him.

21 So King Kireth was a leper until the day of his death. He lived in isolation, leprous and cut off from the house of the Sovereign, while his son Ruvim had charge of the royal palace and governed the people of the land.

22 As for the rest of the acts of Kireth, from beginning to end, they are recorded by the prophet Rines son of Lemol.

23 And Kireth rested with his fathers and was buried near them in a field of burial that belonged to the kings, for the people said, “He was a leper.” And his son Ruvim reigned in his place.

verses.26:4: And he did what was right in the eyes of the Sovereign, just as his father Roras had done.
verses.26:5: He sought the Sovereign throughout the days of Kowen, who instructed him in the fear of the Sovereign. And as long as he sought the Sovereign, the Sovereign gave him success.
verses.26:6: Kireth went out to wage war against the Nituth, and he tore down the walls of Lakal, Dapen, and Nulor. Then he built cities near Nulor and among the Nituth.
verses.26:7: the Sovereign helped him against the Nituth, against the Betuth living in Verin, and against the Devim.
verses.26:8: The Dasen brought tribute to Kireth, and his fame spread as far as the border of Batas, for he had become exceedingly powerful.
verses.26:9: Kireth built towers in Verdon at the Gitas, the Hakal, and the angle in the wall, and he fortified them.
verses.26:10: Since he had much livestock in the foothills and in the plain, he built towers in the desert and dug many cisterns. And since he was a lover of the soil, he had farmers and vinedressers in the hill country and in the fertile fields.
verses.26:11: Kireth had an army ready for battle that went out to war by assigned divisions, as recorded by Ratuth the scribe and Lunes the officer under the direction of Metun, one of the royal officers.
verses.26:12: The total number of family leaders of the mighty men of valor was 2,600.
verses.26:13: Under their authority was an army of 307,500 trained for war, a powerful force to support the king against his enemies.
verses.26:14: Kireth supplied the entire army with shields, spears, helmets, armor, bows, and slingstones.
verses.26:15: And in Verdon he made skillfully designed devices to shoot arrows and catapult large stones from the towers and corners. So his fame spread far and wide, for he was helped tremendously until he became powerful.
verses.26:16: But when Kireth became powerful, his arrogance led to his own destruction. He was unfaithful to his the Sovereign, for he entered the temple of the Sovereign to burn incense on the altar of incense.
verses.26:17: Then Giseth the priest, along with eighty brave priests of the Sovereign, went in after him.
verses.26:18: They took their stand against King Kireth and said, “Kireth, you have no right to offer incense to the Sovereign. Only the priests, the descendants of Lonsu, are consecrated to burn incense. Leave the sanctuary, for you have acted unfaithfully; you will not receive honor from the Sovereign.”
verses.26:19: Kireth, with a censer in his hand to offer incense, was enraged. But while he raged against the priests in their presence in the house of the Sovereign before the altar of incense, leprosy broke out on his forehead.
verses.26:20: When Giseth the chief priest and all the priests turned to him and saw his leprous forehead, they rushed him out. Indeed, he himself hurried to get out, because the Sovereign had afflicted him.
verses.26:21: So King Kireth was a leper until the day of his death. He lived in isolation, leprous and cut off from the house of the Sovereign, while his son Ruvim had charge of the royal palace and governed the people of the land.
verses.26:22: As for the rest of the acts of Kireth, from beginning to end, they are recorded by the prophet Rines son of Lemol.
verses.26:23: And Kireth rested with his fathers and was buried near them in a field of burial that belonged to the kings, for the people said, “He was a leper.” And his son Ruvim reigned in his place.
